link.title: Probability Distributions
link.description: A distribution is how probability is spread over the values a random variable can take. This module works one lecture at a time from the ground up: the three functions that describe any distribution (PMF, PDF, CDF), the discrete family (Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson), the continuous family (Normal, Standard Normal & z-scores, Uniform, Log-Normal), the heavy-tailed family (Power Law, Pareto) that finance actually lives in, and finally the two ideas that connect a sample back to reality — the Central Limit Theorem and estimation. Every page has an interactive lab or 3D visual and a runnable example. (Study reference: the 'Probability Distribution Functions' section of a Complete Data Science bootcamp — all notes, code, and visuals are my own.)
